excluded_setup_run.reason: The disposable mounted cache directory was not writable by the Renovate container user, so no repository scan completed. The lab was corrected before the valid run.

configuration.selection: Nested deterministic subsets ordered by SHA-256 of repository name
configuration.credential: GitHub App installation token scoped to the exact cohort with read-only repository permissions
configuration.execution: One Renovate process per cohort; cold scan followed by a warm-cache scan; cohorts executed serially

observed_update_heavy_mix.meaning: Fit across the four cold scans. It describes this historical lab mixture, in which many repositories repeatedly simulated pending Copier and lockfile updates.

no_expensive_update_scenario.meaning: Scenario estimate based on observed init, extract and lookup phases at 84 repositories, with expensive update work removed. It is not a measured capacity limit.

interpretation.dominant_variable: The amount of active update work, especially Copier execution and lockfile regeneration, dominated runtime more than repository count alone.
interpretation.cache: Keeping the datasource cache between the two scans reduced the 84-repository scan by 25 seconds but did not remove repeated update work.
interpretation.api: GitHub core API quota was not the limiting resource in the measured range.

limitations: The 84 repositories are heterogeneous historical lab sandboxes, not a representative production fleet sample.

dryRun=full does not persist branches or pull requests, so each pass simulated all updates that remained available. This creates an intentionally update-heavy workload compared with a converged fleet.
Repository contents, active updates, Copier and lockfile commands, registries, GitHub latency and runner load can change runtime.
The scenario estimates are planning evidence, not guarantees and not an architecture decision.
Event coalescing and replacement of pending GitHub Actions runs were not tested by this experiment.
